title: Microsoft Foundry: ground agents in SharePoint files through the SharePoint tool
summary: Hold: the summary promises that nothing is forced on administrators while the body correctly says tenant-level arrival behaviour is not stated. The pay-as-you-go prerequisites also omit the required Owner or Contributor access on an Azure subscription in good standing; the roadmap facts and published retrieval pricing are supported.

claims.claim: Foundry role assignments are managed in Azure portal at Foundry resource > Access control (IAM).
claims.quote: In the Azure portal, open your Foundry resource and go to Access control (IAM). Create a role assignment for Foundry User, set Members to User, group, or service principal, select your user principal, and then select Review + assign.
claims.fix: The path stops on the correct IAM page. Keep it and append to controls[0].note: 'In IAM, create a role assignment for Foundry User, set Members to User, group, or service principal, select the user principal, then select Review + assign.' These are the remaining steps at https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry.

claims.claim: Foundry Agent Consumer is documented as a least-privilege role for users who only interact with agents.
claims.quote: If a user or service principal only needs to interact with agents (for example, calling the Responses API) without creating or modifying them, assign Foundry Agent Consumer instead of Foundry User. This role provides least-privilege access for agent consumers.

claims.claim: The SharePoint tool page does not state that Foundry Agent Consumer is sufficient for that tool.
claims.quote: Searched: "SharePoint tool" "Foundry Agent Consumer". Read SharePoint tool prerequisites and RBAC agent-consumer passages. The tool requires at least Foundry User; the RBAC page's generic least-privilege recommendation does not explicitly address this tool.
